edition_angle: Aging dampens the synchronized hemodynamic and cerebrospinal fluid waves during sleep, compromising the brain's essential nightly waste-clearing mechanism.

assignments.angle: Living Waters / Luminous Mind: Age-related reduction in sleep-driven hemodynamic and cerebrospinal fluid flow waves reveals a structural decline in the brain's nightly clearance dynamics.
assignments.reason: This primary study published in Nature Aging pinpoints a fundamental biophysical mechanism—reduced hemodynamic and CSF flow oscillations during sleep—which underpins neurovascular coupling and glymphatic clearance in the aging brain.
